title: Dave Ananth tax site — governed page copy (src/data/pages.yaml)

title.comment: The WordPress page title, decoded. /articles/ takes its <h1> and <title> from the `articles-advice` record.

description.comment: The WordPress excerpt rendered to plain text. Upstream copy, preserved as-is including its truncation artefacts. Used as the meta description; never rewritten to read better.

href.comment: Wider than the href rule in schemas/site.v1.schema.json because migrated page copy also links to site-root paths ("/about") alongside anchors, absolute URLs, mailto: and tel:.

allOf.comment: Every section must carry something renderable.
items is only valid on a list section.
A quote section requires body — the quoted text itself.

ATTRIBUTION. On a quote, `heading` is the attributed name and `meta` the secondary attribution line (e.g. "August 2026"). A meta without a heading would print a date under an anonymous testimonial, so meta requires heading.
meta is only valid on a quote section.
A cta section requires body — the link label.
href is only valid on a cta section. A cta WITHOUT an href is a form submit button, which has no target of its own — so href stays optional on cta.

comment: Platform-facing mirror of `pagesSchema` in src/data/schema.ts, which is the enforcing validator: every strictObject rejects unknown keys, and `superRefine` enforces the seven cross-field rules restated above as if/then. Every one of the nine WordPress slugs is required and no others are allowed — a page that silently stops being migrated is a content regression, not a smaller file. The copy inside is verbatim client copy: attribution lines (testimonial names and dates, source links) are load-bearing and must never be stripped or paraphrased, and no length cap or punctuation normalisation is applied anywhere, because every string must survive the round-trip unchanged.
